name: Niacinamide
lead: Niacinamide (nicotinamide) is the amide form of vitamin B3 and a staple ingredient in cosmetic serums and moisturizers. Typical claims include improved barrier function, reduced oil appearance and pore prominence, calmer redness and a more even tone.
Clinical studies support modest benefits for hyperpigmentation, barrier function and some inflammatory acne, but effect sizes are generally small and vary between formulations.

paras: Niacinamide is a precursor of NAD+ and NADP+, coenzymes central to cellular energy and repair. In skin it increases ceramide and barrier lipid synthesis, reduces sebum output and interferes with the transfer of melanosomes from melanocytes to keratinocytes, helping to lighten uneven pigment.

It is generally very well tolerated. Occasional flushing, itching or irritation occurs, especially at higher concentrations or in poorly formulated products. It is sold freely as a cosmetic ingredient.
